rationale: The previous candidate showed good balance and was approved for racing, but the race data revealed specific weaknesses: the robot stalled on the slalom track (0% finish rate, 2 line loss events on average), and the s-bend track had a low finish rate (35%) with relatively high control effort and steering oscillation. The oval track performed best but still had some off-track events. To address these issues, I reduced the derivative gain kd from 3 to 2.5 to smooth steering and reduce oscillations, as suggested by the evaluator. I increased the integral gain ki from 0.5 to 0.7 to improve steady-state error correction, which should reduce rms_error and help maintain line tracking. I also lowered the base_speed from 1.5 to 1.3 to improve stability and reduce stalling, especially on the challenging slalom track. The geometry remains unchanged since it was well balanced and stable. I kept the sensor layout and weights the same, as they matched successful patterns. I continue to request the same measurements to monitor completion, progress, errors, line loss, and steering oscillation. I expect these changes to improve finish rates on the s-bend and slalom tracks by reducing stalls and oscillations, while maintaining good speed and line tracking on the oval track.
